0.title: About Augustus
0.content: Augustus is a free, open-source re-implementation of a classic Roman city-building game. @PThis copy is running on freely made replacement data: the texts, pictures and sounds were created from scratch for this purpose and are not the originals. @PBuild a thriving city, keep your people fed, healthy and entertained, and earn the favour of Rome.
0.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ABOUT (0): top menu Help > About, and advisor windows without own help. If image.id is non-zero for id 0 the dialog draws image_group(GROUP_BIG_PEOPLE) instead of a message image.

1.title: Workshops
1.content: Workshops turn raw materials into finished goods. A potter needs clay, a brickworks needs clay and straw-like fillers, and a concrete maker needs sand and water. @PRaw materials are delivered from a nearby producer or warehouse. Finished goods go to a warehouse, where markets, traders or other workshops can collect them.
1.notes: help_id 1: pottery workshop, brickworks, concrete maker info windows (window/building/industry.c).

2.title: Market
2.content: A market sends a buyer to fetch food and goods from granaries and warehouses, and a trader who walks the streets selling them to houses. @PPlace markets close to housing and within reach of your storage buildings.

3.title: Granary
3.content: A granary stores food delivered from farms, wharves and traders. Market buyers collect food here. @PUse the special orders to choose which foods are accepted, or to empty the granary.
3.notes: help_id 3: granary, granary orders; also used by roadblock orders and non-dock trade buildings.

4.title: Warehouse
4.content: A warehouse stores raw materials and finished goods. It supplies workshops, markets and traders, and is where Rome's requests are collected from. @PSpecial orders let you decide which goods each warehouse accepts.

5.title: Basics
5.content: Every city starts with roads. Lay a road network first, then mark out housing plots next to it. Settlers will arrive along the road from the edge of the map and move in. @PNew homes need water, food and services to grow. Build wells or fountains nearby, set up farms, a granary and a market, and add a prefecture and an engineer's post to guard against fire and decay. @PWatch the advisors: they tell you what your people lack and how Rome judges your work.
5.notes: Extra manual topic (unused id) linked from the help index (10).

6.title: Desirability
6.content: Some buildings make a neighbourhood more pleasant, others make it worse. Gardens, statues, temples and plazas raise desirability; workshops, farms, mines and barracks lower it. @PFine houses only develop in desirable areas, so keep noisy industry away from your best districts and decorate wealthy streets with greenery.
6.notes: Extra manual topic (unused id) linked from the help index (10).

7.title: Fire and Collapse
7.content: Buildings slowly become a fire risk and a collapse risk as time passes. Prefects walking past a building reset its fire risk; engineers reset its damage. @PPlace prefectures and engineer's posts throughout the city so that their walkers pass every street regularly. Use the risk overlays to find buildings in danger.
7.notes: Extra manual topic (unused id) linked from the help index (10).

8.title: Mission Post
8.content: Missionaries from this post visit the native villages around your city, teaching them Roman ways and keeping them peaceful.

9.title: The Gods
9.content: Five gods watch over your city: Ceres (farming), Neptune (the sea), Mercury (commerce), Mars (war) and Venus (love and happiness). @PEach god wants temples and festivals in proportion to the size of your city. A pleased god may grant a blessing; a neglected god grows angry and will eventually strike the city.
9.notes: Extra manual topic (unused id) linked from the help index (10).

10.content: Welcome to the governor's handbook. Click on a red word to open that topic. @PGetting started: @5Basics @LHousing and land value: @56Housing, @6Desirability @LSupplies: @12Food, @62Water, @60Aqueducts, @2Markets, @3Granaries, @4Warehouses @LWork: @13Employment, @46Industry @LSafety: @7Fire, @86Prefectures, @81Engineers @LHealth: @63Barbers, @64Baths, @65Doctors, @66Hospitals @LFaith: @67Temples, @9Gods @LLearning: @68Schools, @69Academies, @70Libraries @LEntertainment: @71Theaters, @72Amphitheaters, @73Colosseums, @74Hippodromes @LGovernment: @76Forum, @77Senate, @78Residences, @79Statues, @80Gardens @LTrade: @11Trade, @83Docks, @32Empire @LDefence: @85Walls, @87Forts, @37Barracks, @88Academy @LAdvisors: @20Labor, @21Military, @22Imperial, @23Ratings, @24Trade, @25Population, @26Health, @27Education, @28Entertainment, @29Religion, @30Finance, @31Chief @LInterface: @15Treasury, @16Population, @17Date, @18Overlays, @34Messages
10.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_HELP (10): top menu Help, fallback help for buildings with help_id 0, help button in city messages.

11.title: Trade
11.content: Open trade routes on the empire map to buy goods you cannot make and sell your surplus. Land traders arrive by road; sea traders need a working dock. @PUse the trade advisor to choose which goods are imported or exported and how much to keep in stock. Goods are traded through your warehouses.
11.notes: Extra manual topic (unused id) linked from the help index (10).

12.title: Food
12.content: Farms and wharves produce food. Cart pushers take it to a granary, and market buyers fetch it from the granary to sell to nearby houses. @PLarger houses want more than one kind of food. A steady, varied supply keeps people healthy and lets them move up in the world.
12.notes: Extra manual topic (unused id) linked from the help index (10).

13.title: Employment
13.content: Almost every building needs workers, and workers come from houses that a recruiter can reach by road. @PIf jobs outnumber workers, some buildings will stand idle. If workers outnumber jobs, unemployment makes people unhappy. Use the labor advisor to set priorities between categories.
13.notes: Extra manual topic (unused id) linked from the help index (10).

15.title: Treasury
15.content: This figure shows the money held by the city. Construction, wages and festivals are paid from it; taxes and exports fill it again. @PIf the treasury runs dry you can go into debt for a short while, but Rome will not tolerate it for long.
15.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_TOP_FUNDS (15): right-click the funds display in the top menu bar.

16.title: Population
16.content: This is the number of people living in your city. Population grows when housing has room and the city is attractive to newcomers, and shrinks when people are unhappy or homes are destroyed.
16.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_TOP_POPULATION (16): right-click the population display in the top menu bar.

17.title: Date
17.content: The current month and year. Taxes and wages are settled once a year, and many events, requests and deadlines are tied to the calendar.
17.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_TOP_DATE (17): right-click the date display in the top menu bar.

18.title: Overlays
18.content: Overlays colour the map to show one aspect of the city at a time, such as fire risk, water coverage, access to services or desirability. Choose an overlay from the button above the sidebar; choose it again or select 'none' to return to the normal view.
18.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_OVERLAYS (18): right-click the overlay button on the sidebar.

20.title: Labor Advisor
20.content: The labor advisor shows how many people are employed, how many are looking for work and how workers are spread across the sectors of the economy. @PRaise a sector's priority to make sure it is staffed first. You can also change the wage level; better pay attracts settlers but costs the treasury.
20.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_LABOR (20): help button in the labor advisor.

21.title: Military Advisor
21.content: The military advisor lists your legions with their strength, morale and current orders, and warns of approaching enemies. @PFrom here you can send soldiers home to their fort, out to the city, or away to help the empire.
21.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_MILITARY (21): help button in the military advisor.

22.title: Imperial Advisor
22.content: The imperial advisor shows your standing with the emperor and any outstanding requests from Rome. @PDispatch requested goods or money before the deadline to gain favour. You may also send personal gifts and set your own salary here; an extravagant salary will not be popular in Rome.
22.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_IMPERIAL (22): help button in the imperial advisor.

23.title: Ratings Advisor
23.content: Four ratings measure your success: culture, prosperity, peace and favour. Each mission sets targets that must be reached to win. @PClick on a rating to hear what affects it and how you might improve it.
23.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_RATINGS (23): help button in the ratings advisor.

24.title: Trade Advisor
24.content: The trade advisor lists every good, how much is in your warehouses, and whether it is being imported, exported or kept. @PClick a good to change its trade setting, to stockpile it, or to stop industry producing it.
24.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_TRADE (24): help button in the trade advisor.

25.title: Population Advisor
25.content: The population advisor shows the age structure of your citizens, the kinds of housing they live in and the city's food supply. @PA healthy city has plenty of working-age people and enough housing room for new arrivals.
25.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_POPULATION (25): help button in the population and housing advisors.

26.title: Health Advisor
26.content: The health advisor reports how well your people are served by baths, barbers, doctors and hospitals, and warns about the risk of disease. @PClean water and good food help, but only proper health care prevents outbreaks.
26.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_HEALTH (26): help button in the health advisor.

27.title: Education Advisor
27.content: The education advisor shows how many people can be served by schools, academies and libraries compared with the number who need them. @PEducated citizens are needed before houses can grow into the finest homes.
27.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_EDUCATION (27): help button in the education advisor.

28.title: Entertainment Advisor
28.content: The entertainment advisor shows the coverage of theaters, amphitheaters, colosseums and the hippodrome, and lets you plan games. @PPeople expect more entertainment as their houses grow; a lack of it makes them restless.
28.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_ENTERTAINMENT (28): help button in the entertainment advisor and the hold games window.

29.title: Religion Advisor
29.content: The religion advisor shows each god's mood, the temples built in their honour and the festivals held. @PKeep every god content. Holding a festival is a quick way to soothe an angry god.
29.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_RELIGION (29): help button in the religion advisor and the hold festival window.

30.title: Financial Advisor
30.content: The financial advisor shows the money coming in and going out this year and last year, and lets you set the tax rate. @PTaxes are only collected from houses visited by a tax collector from a forum or senate.
30.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_FINANCIAL (30): help button in the financial advisor.

31.title: Chief Advisor
31.content: The chief advisor gives a summary of the most pressing matters in the city: jobs, food, health, crime, religion and military threats. Start here when something seems wrong.
31.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_ADVISOR_CHIEF (31): help button in the chief advisor.

32.title: The Empire
32.content: The empire map shows your province, Rome and the other cities of the empire. Click a city to see what it buys and sells and what it costs to open a trade route. @PEnemy armies and distant battles may also be shown here.
32.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_EMPIRE_MAP (32): help button on the empire map, right-click the empire button on the sidebar.

34.title: Messages
34.content: The message list keeps every report sent to you. Unread messages are highlighted. Click a message to read it again, or right-click to delete it.
34.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_MESSAGES (34): help in the message list, right-click the messages button on the sidebar.

37.title: Barracks
37.content: The barracks trains new soldiers for your forts and sends them out as they are needed. It requires weapons to equip soldiers for the heavier legions. @PWithout a working barracks, forts cannot replace their losses.

42.title: Citizens
42.content: The people of the city each have a job to do: prefects, engineers, priests, cart pushers, traders and many more walk the streets. Click on a walker to see who they are, where they are going and what they think of life in your city.
42.notes: help_id 42: info window for a figure (walker) on a tile (window/building/terrain.c). Note: ships and other figure types >= FIGURE_SHIPWRECK use help_id 330, which lies in the Augustus-managed range.

46.title: Industry Orders
46.content: This window controls a single good. You can turn production of it on or off for the whole city, choose whether it is traded, and set how much should be kept in storage before any is sold.
46.notes: MESSAGE_DIALOG_INDUSTRY (46): help button in the resource settings window (window/resource_settings.c).

56.title: Housing
56.content: Houses start as simple tents and can grow into grand villas. Each step up needs better access to water, food, goods, services and a more desirable neighbourhood. @PClick on a house to see what it needs in order to evolve. If its needs are no longer met, it will slowly decline again.

57.title: Roads
57.content: Roads connect every part of your city. Walkers, carts and traders travel along them, and most buildings only work if they are next to a road. @PPlazas can be laid on roads to make them more attractive.

58.title: Bridges
58.content: Bridges carry roads across rivers. Low bridges are cheap but block ships; ship bridges are taller and let boats pass underneath.

59.title: Reservoir
59.content: A reservoir collects water and feeds it into aqueducts and fountains. It must be built next to fresh water or connected by aqueduct to another full reservoir. @PReservoirs also water the land around them.

60.title: Aqueduct
60.content: Aqueducts carry water from a reservoir across the land to other reservoirs and fountains. Roads may pass under an aqueduct, but not over the ends.
60.notes: help_id 60: aqueduct building and aqueduct terrain info.

61.title: Fountain
61.content: A fountain gives clean water to houses nearby. It needs a full reservoir connected by pipes underground and a worker to tend it.

62.title: Well
62.content: A well draws groundwater for the houses around it. It is cheap and needs no workers, but the water is not as good as that from a fountain.

63.title: Barber
63.content: Barbers keep citizens neat and tidy. Better homes will not develop without a barber's visits.

64.title: Bathhouse
64.content: A bathhouse lets people bathe and relax, improving hygiene. It must be supplied with water from a reservoir to operate.

65.title: Doctor
65.content: A doctor's clinic sends a physician through the streets to treat the sick and keep illness from spreading.

66.title: Hospital
66.content: A hospital cares for the sick of the whole city. Larger cities need hospital beds to keep disease away.

67.title: Temples
67.content: Temples honour the gods and send priests into the streets. Each god needs temples in proportion to the size of your city. @PLarge temples and oracles please the gods more. Small shrines and household altars bring religion to quiet corners of the city.
67.notes: help_id 67: small/large temples, oracle, lararium, shrine, nymphaeum, mausoleums.

68.title: School
68.content: A school sends a schoolmaster to teach the children of nearby houses. Basic education is needed for houses to grow beyond the middle ranks.

69.title: Academy
69.content: The academy teaches older students and brings higher learning to the finest neighbourhoods.

70.title: Library
70.content: A library lends scrolls to citizens, giving them knowledge and culture. Wealthy households expect access to a library.

71.title: Theater
71.content: Actors from an actor colony perform plays at the theater. It is the simplest form of entertainment and pleasant for any neighbourhood.

72.title: Amphitheater
72.content: The amphitheater hosts both actors and gladiators, entertaining a larger crowd than a theater.

73.title: Colosseum
73.content: The colosseum stages gladiator fights and wild animal shows for a large part of the city. It needs both gladiators and lions to put on a full programme.
73.notes: help_id 73: colosseum and arena info windows.

74.title: Hippodrome
74.content: The hippodrome hosts chariot races, the grandest entertainment of all. Only one can be built in a city.

75.title: Training Schools
75.content: Performers have to be trained before they can entertain. The actor colony, gladiator school, lion house and chariot maker each send their pupils to the venues that need them.
75.notes: help_id 75: actor colony, gladiator school, lion house, chariot maker.

76.title: Forum
76.content: The forum sends tax collectors into the city. Only houses they visit pay taxes.

77.title: Senate
77.content: The senate is the seat of city government. It collects taxes like a forum and raises the city's standing. Only one senate can be built.

78.title: Governor's Residence
78.content: Your personal home in the city. A grander residence adds to the beauty of its neighbourhood and is paid for from your own savings as well as the city treasury.
78.notes: help_id 78: governor's house / villa / palace info windows.

79.title: Statues and Monuments
79.content: Statues, obelisks and triumphal arches decorate the city and make surrounding land more desirable.

80.title: Gardens and Plazas
80.content: Gardens, ponds and plazas make nearby houses more pleasant to live in. They cost little and need no workers.

81.title: Engineer's Post
81.content: Engineers walk the streets inspecting buildings and repairing damage before anything collapses.

82.title: Shipyard
82.content: The shipyard uses timber to build fishing boats for your wharves.

83.title: Dock
83.content: Sea traders unload and load their cargo at a dock. A dock needs workers and road access to your warehouses.

84.title: Wharf
84.content: A wharf is the home port of a fishing boat. The catch is taken to a granary as food. The boat itself comes from a shipyard.

85.title: Walls and Towers
85.content: Walls, palisades, towers and gatehouses protect the city from attack. Towers are manned by sentries who fire at enemies within range.
85.notes: help_id 85: walls, palisades, towers, gatehouses, watchtower and wall terrain info.

86.title: Prefecture
86.content: Prefects patrol the streets, putting out fires, deterring crime and reducing the risk of fire in the buildings they pass.

87.title: Forts and Legions
87.content: A fort houses a legion. Soldiers are trained at the barracks and march to their fort when ready. Select a legion's standard to give it orders.
87.notes: help_id 87: fort and legion info windows.

88.title: Military Academy
88.content: The military academy gives new recruits extra training, so they join their legion with higher skill.

89.title: Wheat Farm
89.content: A wheat farm grows grain on fertile land. The harvest is carted to a granary to feed the city.

90.title: Food Farms
90.content: Vegetable farms, fruit orchards and pig farms add variety to the diet. They need fertile land and send their produce to the granaries.
90.notes: help_id 90: vegetable farm, fruit farm, pig farm info windows.

91.title: Olive and Vine Farms
91.content: Olive groves and vineyards grow raw materials for oil and wine. Their crops go to workshops or to a warehouse for trade.
91.notes: help_id 91: olive farm and vine farm info windows.

92.title: Clay Pit
92.content: Workers dig clay here for potters and brick makers. Clay pits are best placed near water.

93.title: Mines and Pits
93.content: Mines and quarries extract iron, gold, stone and sand from the rocky ground. The material is carried to workshops or warehouses.
93.notes: help_id 93: iron mine, gold mine, stone quarry, sand pit info windows.

94.title: Timber Yard
94.content: Woodcutters fell trees near the timber yard and send the logs on to furniture workshops, shipyards or warehouses.

95.title: Marble Quarry
95.content: Marble is cut from rocky outcrops and used for large temples, monuments and the oracle.

96.title: Wine Workshop
96.content: The wine workshop presses grapes from the vineyards into wine, a luxury wanted by the finest houses.

97.title: Oil Workshop
97.content: The oil workshop presses olives into oil for lamps and cooking. Many houses need oil to develop.

98.title: Weapons Workshop
98.content: The weapons workshop forges iron into weapons for your barracks or for trade.

99.title: Furniture Workshop
99.content: Carpenters at the furniture workshop turn timber into furniture, needed for comfortable homes.

101.title: Population 500
101.content: Our settlement has grown to five hundred souls. Word of a new town is starting to spread.

102.title: Population 1000
102.content: A thousand citizens now call this place home. It is beginning to look like a real town.

103.title: Population 2000
103.content: The population has reached two thousand. Traders and craftsmen are taking notice.

104.title: Population 3000
104.content: Three thousand people now live here. Keep the food and water flowing to sustain this growth.

105.title: Population 5000
105.content: With five thousand inhabitants the town has become a city of note in the province.

106.title: Population 10000
106.content: Ten thousand citizens! The city is now one of the largest in the region.

107.title: Population 15000
107.content: Fifteen thousand people fill the streets. Even senators in Rome have heard of the city.

108.title: Population 20000
108.content: Twenty thousand inhabitants. The city rivals the great centres of the empire.

109.title: Population 25000
109.content: Twenty-five thousand citizens. Few cities outside Rome itself can claim such a size.

110.title: Riot
110.content: Angry citizens have taken to the streets and set a building alight. Unhappiness and crime are out of hand. @PImprove living conditions and build more prefectures to restore order.
110.notes: MESSAGE_RIOT (11): param1 = building type (shown in header), param2 = grid offset.

111.title: Fire
111.content: A building has burned down. Fire spreads quickly, so make sure prefects patrol every street.
111.notes: MESSAGE_FIRE (12): param1 = building type, param2 = grid offset.

112.title: Building Collapse
112.content: A building has collapsed into rubble. Engineers must inspect buildings regularly to prevent this.
112.notes: MESSAGE_COLLAPSED_BUILDING (13): param1 = building type, param2 = grid offset.

113.title: Building Destroyed
113.content: Rioters or enemies have destroyed a building in the city.
113.notes: MESSAGE_DESTROYED_BUILDING (14): param1 = building type, param2 = grid offset (figuretype/crime.c).

114.title: Navigation Blocked
114.content: A trade ship cannot reach its dock. Make sure the waterway is not blocked by low bridges or other obstacles.
114.notes: MESSAGE_NAVIGATION_IMPOSSIBLE (15): sea trader cannot reach a dock.

115.title: City in Debt
115.content: The city treasury is empty and the city is in debt. Rome has covered the shortfall this time, but your prosperity rating has suffered. @PRaise taxes or cut spending at once.

116.title: In Debt Again
116.content: Once again the city has run out of money. The emperor is losing patience with your management of the finances.

117.title: Still in Debt
117.content: The city remains in debt. Every month this continues, the emperor thinks less of you. Restore the treasury before it is too late.

118.title: Caesar's Wrath
118.content: The emperor has run out of patience. Legions are being sent to remove you from office by force.
118.notes: MESSAGE_CAESAR_WRATH (19): defined but not posted by current code (may be posted via scenario 'send standard message').

119.title: Imperial Legions Advance
119.content: The emperor's legions continue their march on the city. Only a great improvement in your favour with Rome will stop them now.

120.title: Imperial Legions Withdraw
120.content: Your favour with Rome has improved and the emperor has recalled his legions. Do not test his patience again.

121.title: Uprising
121.content: Local tribesmen have risen up against Roman rule and are marching on the city. Prepare your defences.
121.notes: MESSAGE_LOCAL_UPRISING (22): param1 = invasion id, param2 = grid offset.

122.title: Invasion
122.content: A hostile army has crossed into the province and is heading for the city. Rally your legions and man the walls.
122.notes: MESSAGE_BARBARIAN_ATTACK (23): param1 = invasion id, param2 = grid offset.

123.title: Imperial Army Arrives
123.content: The emperor's legions have arrived to remove you from office. Fight them off, or win back Rome's favour quickly.
123.notes: MESSAGE_CAESAR_ARMY_ATTACK (24): param1 = invasion id, param2 = grid offset.

124.title: Distant Battle
124.content: Enemies threaten a city elsewhere in the empire. Rome may soon ask you to send troops to its aid.
124.notes: MESSAGE_DISTANT_BATTLE (25): invasion warning for a distant battle (scenario/invasion.c), no popup.

125.title: Enemies Approaching
125.content: Scouts report an enemy force gathering beyond the borders. It will reach us in a year or two.
125.notes: MESSAGE_ENEMIES_CLOSING (26): invasion warning, more than a year away.

126.title: Enemies at the Gates
126.content: An enemy army is almost upon us. It will arrive within the year. Prepare the defences now.
126.notes: MESSAGE_ENEMIES_AT_THE_DOOR (27): invasion warning, less than a year away.

127.title: Request from Rome
127.content: The emperor requests a shipment of goods from the city. Have them ready in a warehouse and dispatch them through the imperial advisor before the deadline.
127.notes: MESSAGE_CAESAR_REQUESTS_GOODS (28): param1 = request id; dialog appends amount, resource and months left.

128.title: Request for Money
128.content: The emperor requests a contribution from the city treasury. Send it through the imperial advisor before the deadline.

129.title: Request for Troops
129.content: Rome calls on you to send soldiers to defend the empire. Dispatch a legion from the military advisor as soon as possible.
129.notes: MESSAGE_CAESAR_REQUESTS_ARMY (30): posted with param1 = request id (scenario/request.c) and with 0 for distant battles (scenario/distant_battle.c); kept GENERAL so request 0 is not drawn wrongly for distant battles.

130.title: Reminder from Rome
130.content: The emperor reminds you that his request is still outstanding. Time is running short.

131.title: Request Received
131.content: The emperor thanks you for your prompt delivery. Your favour with Rome has improved.

132.title: Request Overdue
132.content: The deadline for the emperor's request has passed. Rome is displeased, but you may still send it late.
132.notes: MESSAGE_REQUEST_REFUSED (33): param1 = request id, request now overdue.

133.title: Request Ignored
133.content: You have ignored the emperor's request entirely. Your favour with Rome has fallen sharply.
133.notes: MESSAGE_REQUEST_REFUSED_OVERDUE (34): param1 = request id, request ignored.

134.title: Late Delivery
134.content: The emperor has received your shipment, though later than he wished. Your favour has improved a little.

135.title: Unemployment
135.content: Many citizens cannot find work. Idle hands breed discontent and crime. Build more workplaces.
135.notes: MESSAGE_UNEMPLOYMENT (36): defined, not posted directly by current code.

136.title: Workers Needed
136.content: There are not enough workers to staff all buildings. Attract more settlers or adjust labour priorities.

137.title: Small Festival
137.content: The people enjoyed a modest festival in honour of the gods. The chosen god is pleased.

138.title: Large Festival
138.content: A large festival filled the streets with music and feasting. The people and the chosen god are delighted.

139.title: Grand Festival
139.content: The grand festival will be remembered for years. The people cheer your name and the chosen god is overjoyed.

140.title: Wrath of Ceres
140.content: Ceres is furious at your neglect. Blight has struck the farms and the harvest is ruined.

141.title: Wrath of Neptune
141.content: Neptune is angry, but with no ships at sea his anger finds no target. Honour him before he finds one.
141.notes: MESSAGE_WRATH_OF_NEPTUNE_NO_SEA_TRADE (42): Neptune angry but no ships to sink.

142.title: Wrath of Mercury
142.content: Mercury is enraged. Goods have vanished from your granaries and warehouses.

143.title: Wrath of Mars
143.content: Mars is angry, but with no soldiers in the city his wrath passes by. Build him temples before it is too late.

144.title: Wrath of Venus
144.content: Venus is offended. Joy has drained from the city and the people will not be truly happy until she is appeased.

145.title: Citizens Disgruntled
145.content: The people are grumbling and some are leaving the city. The main complaint is shown above.
145.notes: MESSAGE_PEOPLE_DISGRUNTLED (46): param1 = low mood cause; dialog prints the cause text above the content.

146.title: Citizens Unhappy
146.content: Unhappiness is spreading and families are moving away. Address the cause shown above.

147.title: Citizens Angry
147.content: The people are angry and leaving in large numbers. Act quickly before the city empties.

148.title: Food Shortage
148.content: There is not enough food to go around. Build more farms or import food before people go hungry.
148.notes: MESSAGE_NOT_ENOUGH_FOOD (49): defined, not posted directly by current code.

149.title: Food Not Delivered
149.content: Food is not reaching the markets. Check that granaries are staffed and connected to the markets by road.
149.notes: MESSAGE_FOOD_NOT_DELIVERED (50): defined, not posted directly by current code.

200.title: First Steps
200.subtitle: Training assignment, peaceful
200.content: Welcome, governor. Before Rome trusts you with a real province, you must show that you can run a small town. @PLay roads and housing, keep the town safe from fire and crime, and build a senate. Your current goal is shown above.
200.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 0 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

201.title: Feeding the Town
201.subtitle: Training assignment, peaceful
201.content: This town needs a reliable food supply and a little industry. @PBuild farms and a granary, grow the population, and make pottery for your people and for trade. Your current goal is shown above.
201.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 1 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

202.title: A Quiet Valley
202.subtitle: Assignment 3, peaceful
202.content: A fertile valley awaits settlement. There is little danger here, so concentrate on building a healthy, well-supplied city that meets the goals set by Rome.
202.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 2 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

203.title: The Frontier Post
203.subtitle: Assignment 3, military
203.content: This settlement lies close to unfriendly tribes. Grow the town, but build walls and a fort early. Raids are expected.
203.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 3 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

204.title: River Town
204.subtitle: Assignment 4, peaceful
204.content: A broad river runs through this land. Use it for water and trade, and turn the town into a busy market centre.
204.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 4 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

205.title: Hill Fort
205.subtitle: Assignment 4, military
205.content: Enemies roam the hills around this site. Secure the city with towers and soldiers while it grows.
205.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 5 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

206.title: The Coast
206.subtitle: Assignment 5, peaceful
206.content: A sheltered harbour offers rich opportunities for sea trade. Build docks and workshops and grow wealthy on commerce.
206.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 6 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

207.title: Border Garrison
207.subtitle: Assignment 5, military
207.content: The border must be held. A strong legion and good defences matter as much here as housing and food.
207.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 7 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

208.title: Land of Olives
208.subtitle: Assignment 6, peaceful
208.content: Olive groves and vineyards thrive in this warm province. Develop industry and trade to build a prosperous city.
208.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 8 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

209.title: Contested Plains
209.subtitle: Assignment 6, military
209.content: Rival peoples claim these plains. Expect repeated attacks and keep your legions ready.
209.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 9 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

210.title: The Desert Edge
210.subtitle: Assignment 7, peaceful
210.content: Water is scarce at the edge of the desert. Plan reservoirs and aqueducts carefully to sustain a large population.
210.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 10 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

211.title: Northern Marches
211.subtitle: Assignment 7, military
211.content: Cold forests hide hostile tribes. Build a disciplined army and protect your citizens through the long campaign.
211.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 11 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

212.title: Island Colony
212.subtitle: Assignment 8, peaceful
212.content: This island has little farmland. Rely on fishing and trade to feed a growing city.
212.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 12 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

213.title: Mountain Pass
213.subtitle: Assignment 8, military
213.content: Whoever holds this pass controls the region. Fortify it and drive back every invader.
213.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 13 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

214.title: Grain Province
214.subtitle: Assignment 9, peaceful
214.content: Rome depends on grain from this province. Expect many requests from the emperor and keep your granaries full.
214.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 14 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

215.title: Eastern Frontier
215.subtitle: Assignment 9, military
215.content: Powerful armies threaten the eastern border. Build several forts and a strong economy to pay for them.
215.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 15 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

216.title: Jewel of the Province
216.subtitle: Assignment 10, peaceful
216.content: Build a city of culture and beauty, with fine temples, schools and entertainment, to impress Rome.
216.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 16 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

217.title: Rebel Country
217.subtitle: Assignment 10, military
217.content: The province has risen in revolt. Restore order, defend the city and win back the loyalty of its people.
217.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 17 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

218.title: The Great Port
218.subtitle: Assignment 11, peaceful
218.content: Turn this harbour into the greatest trading city of the empire. Prosperity is the measure of success here.
218.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 18 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

219.title: Siege Lands
219.subtitle: Assignment 11, military
219.content: Enemies will besiege this city again and again. Only strong walls and stronger legions will save it.
219.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 19 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

220.title: The Final Charge
220.subtitle: Final assignment, peaceful
220.content: This is your greatest task. Build a magnificent city that meets every goal Rome sets, and your name will be remembered.
220.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 20 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

221.title: The Last Stand
221.subtitle: Final assignment, military
221.content: The empire's fate hangs on this city. Build, defend and triumph against the mightiest foes you have faced.
221.notes: Mission briefing for campaign mission 21 (window/mission_briefing.c: text_id = 200 + scenario_campaign_mission()). Only title, subtitle and content are used; subtitle must not be null (drawn unconditionally).

251.title: Theft
251.content: A thief has stolen money from the city treasury. Crime grows where people are unhappy and prefects are scarce.
251.notes: MESSAGE_THEFT (52) = MESSAGE_DIALOG_THEFT (251): param1 = denarii stolen (header shows amount), param2 = grid offset.

252.title: Fire!
252.content: A fire has broken out. Fires start in buildings that have not been visited by a prefect for a long time. @PBuild a prefecture near your houses. Its prefect will walk the streets, lower the fire risk and put out any flames. Prefectures are now available in the security menu.

253.title: Collapse!
253.content: A building has collapsed. Old buildings decay unless an engineer inspects them. @PBuild an engineer's post so that engineers patrol the city and keep buildings in good repair. The engineer's post is now available in the engineering menu.

254.title: Gods Unhappy
254.content: The gods feel neglected. Build temples and hold festivals before their displeasure turns to anger.

255.title: Water
255.content: Well done, the granary is filling up. Next, your people need clean water. @PBuild a reservoir by a river or lake and run aqueducts to more reservoirs, then place fountains near your houses. Wells are a cheaper alternative where fountains cannot reach.
255.notes: MESSAGE_TUTORIAL_WATER (56): tutorial 2, after the first granary fills.

256.title: Growing Your City
256.content: The city has passed two hundred and fifty people. To keep growing, houses need more services. @PTemples, schools and entertainment are now available. Place them where their walkers can reach your homes.

257.title: Hunger Halts Immigration
257.content: Settlers will not come to a city that cannot feed them. Make sure your farms, granaries and markets keep food flowing to every house.

258.title: Religion
258.content: The senate is built and the city is taking shape. Do not forget the gods. @PEvery god expects temples. Build at least one for each god and watch their moods in the religion advisor.
258.notes: MESSAGE_TUTORIAL_RELIGION (59): tutorial 1, after the senate is built or population almost reached.

259.title: Taxes and Industry
259.content: With four hundred and fifty citizens it is time to earn some money. @PBuild a forum so that tax collectors can visit your houses. Then set up clay pits and a pottery workshop; pottery is needed by better homes and can be sold to other cities.

260.title: Trade
260.content: Your first pottery has been made. Surplus goods can be sold to other cities of the empire. @POpen the empire map, open a trade route and set pottery to export in the trade advisor. Traders will collect it from your warehouse.
260.notes: MESSAGE_TUTORIAL_TRADE (61): tutorial 2, first pottery stored in a warehouse.

261.title: Earthquake
261.content: An earthquake has torn open the ground and destroyed buildings in its path. The damaged area is impassable.
261.notes: MESSAGE_EARTHQUAKE (62): param1 = 0, param2 = grid offset of the quake.

262.title: Gladiator Revolt
262.content: Gladiators have broken out of their school and are rampaging through the city. Send soldiers to stop them.

263.title: New Emperor
263.content: A new emperor has taken the throne in Rome. Your standing must be earned again from the beginning.

264.title: Land Trade Disrupted
264.content: Sandstorms have closed the desert roads. Land traders will not arrive for some time.

265.title: Sea Trade Disrupted
265.content: Storms and pirates have made the seas unsafe. Sea traders will not arrive for some time.

266.title: Land Trade Disrupted
266.content: Landslides have blocked the mountain passes. Land traders will not arrive for some time.

267.title: Wages Rise in Rome
267.content: Wages in Rome have gone up. Unless you pay as much, workers will be less eager to come here.

268.title: Wages Fall in Rome
268.content: Wages in Rome have gone down. You may be able to lower your own wages without losing workers.

269.title: Contaminated Water
269.content: The water supply has been fouled and sickness is spreading. Health care is needed urgently.

270.title: Mine Collapse
270.content: An iron mine has caved in. The workings have been lost.

271.title: Clay Pit Flooded
271.content: Water has burst into a clay pit and flooded it. The pit can no longer be worked.

272.title: Revolt Ended
272.content: The gladiator revolt is over and order has returned to the streets.

273.title: Trade Increased
273.content: This city now wants to trade more of this good with us.
273.notes: MESSAGE_INCREASED_TRADING (74): param1 = empire city id (name shown), param2 = resource (icon shown).

274.title: Trade Decreased
274.content: This city now wants to trade less of this good with us.
274.notes: MESSAGE_DECREASED_TRADING (75): param1 = empire city id, param2 = resource.

275.title: Trade Stopped
275.content: This city no longer trades this good with us.
275.notes: MESSAGE_TRADE_STOPPED (76): param1 = empire city id, param2 = resource.

276.title: Empire Expanded
276.content: The empire has grown and new cities are open to trade. Visit the empire map to see what they offer.

277.title: Price Increase
277.content: The price of this good has gone up throughout the empire by the amount shown.
277.notes: MESSAGE_PRICE_INCREASED (78): param1 = amount (drawn as money), param2 = resource.

278.title: Price Decrease
278.content: The price of this good has gone down throughout the empire by the amount shown.

279.title: Road to Rome Blocked
279.content: You may not cut the road linking the city to Rome. The demolition has been stopped.

280.title: Wrath of Neptune
280.content: Neptune's fury has sent our ships to the bottom of the sea.

281.title: Wrath of Mars
281.content: Mars has turned against us and sent enemies to attack the city.

283.title: Battle Lost
283.content: No troops were sent to the distant battle, and the city we were to defend has fallen. Rome is deeply disappointed.

284.title: Battle Lost
284.content: Our legion arrived too late. The enemy had already taken the city.

285.title: Battle Lost
285.content: Our legion fought bravely but was too weak to defeat the enemy.

286.title: Battle Won
286.content: Our legion has defeated the enemy far from home. The emperor is grateful.

287.title: Troops Return
287.content: The survivors of our defeated legion have returned to the city.

288.title: Victorious Troops Return
288.content: Our victorious legion has marched home to a heroes' welcome.

289.title: City Retaken
289.content: Imperial forces have recaptured the city lost in the distant battle. Trade with it can resume.

290.title: Ceres Is Upset
290.content: The fields are withering. Ceres is upset and has spoiled some of the crops. Build temples and hold a festival to calm the god.

291.title: Neptune Is Upset
291.content: A ship has been lost at sea. Neptune is upset with the city. Build temples and hold a festival to calm the god.

292.title: Mercury Is Upset
292.content: Goods have gone missing from storage. Mercury is upset with the city. Build temples and hold a festival to calm the god.

293.title: Mars Is Upset
293.content: Mars is upset and has sent raiders against the city. Build temples and hold a festival to calm the god.

294.title: Venus Is Upset
294.content: The people feel gloomy. Venus is upset with the city. Build temples and hold a festival to calm the god.

295.title: Blessing from Ceres
295.content: Ceres has blessed the farms. Crops are ripening early and the harvest will be rich.

296.title: Blessing from Neptune
296.content: Neptune has blessed the seas. Ships sail swiftly and safely to our docks.

297.title: Blessing from Mercury
297.content: Mercury has blessed our trade and our storehouses are well stocked.

298.title: Blessing from Mars
298.content: Mars has blessed our soldiers. His spirit will defend the city against the next attack.

299.title: Blessing from Venus
299.content: Venus has blessed the city. The people are filled with happiness.

300.title: The Gods Are Angry
300.content: The gods are angry with the city. Disaster will follow unless they are appeased with temples and festivals.

301.title: Illness
301.content: Illness has broken out in the city. Build more doctors and hospitals and keep the water clean.

302.title: Disease
302.content: Disease is spreading through the city. Without better health care, people will die.

303.title: Plague
303.content: Plague is ravaging the city and many have died. Health care must be improved immediately.

304.title: Spirit of Mars
304.content: The spirit of Mars has struck down the invaders. The god's blessing has been spent.

305.title: The Emperor Relents
305.content: The emperor has noted your recent efforts and his anger has cooled. Continue to win back his favour.

306.title: The Emperor Is Impressed
306.content: Your defence of the city has impressed the emperor. He has called off his legions for now.

307.title: The Emperor Yields
307.content: Having failed to remove you, the emperor grudgingly accepts your rule. Your favour has been restored somewhat.

308.title: Hippodrome Open
308.content: The hippodrome is staging its first chariot races. The crowds are thrilled.
308.notes: MESSAGE_WORKING_HIPPODROME (109): original variant (Augustus posts the _NEW variant).

309.title: Colosseum Open
309.content: The colosseum has staged its first games. The whole city is talking about it.

310.title: Citizens Leaving
310.content: People are leaving the city because they are unhappy. The main complaint is shown above.
310.notes: MESSAGE_EMIGRATION (111): param1 = 0 so the dialog shows the current low-mood cause.

311.title: Dismissed
311.content: The emperor has lost all confidence in you and you have been removed from office.

313.title: Enemy Army
313.content: An enemy army has invaded the province and is marching on the city.
313.notes: MESSAGE_ENEMY_ARMY_ATTACK (114): param1 = invasion id, param2 = grid offset.

314.title: Request Can Be Met
314.content: We now have enough in storage to meet the emperor's request. Dispatch it from the imperial advisor.

315.title: Road to Rome Obstructed
315.content: Nothing may be built across the road to Rome. The road must stay open.

316.title: No Working Dock
316.content: Ships want to trade with us, but no dock is ready to receive them. Build or staff a dock.

317.title: Fishing Boat Blocked
317.content: A fishing boat cannot reach the fishing grounds. Clear the waterway.

318.title: Health
318.content: Disease has appeared in the city. Doctors and hospitals keep people healthy, and baths and barbers help too. @PBuild a doctor's clinic near your houses and check the health advisor regularly.

320.title: Uprising
320.content: Mars has stirred the local tribes into revolt. They are marching on the city.
320.notes: MESSAGE_LOCAL_UPRISING_MARS (121): param1 = invasion id, param2 = grid offset.

_format_notes: File layout (core/lang.c parse_message): 24-byte header (skipped), 400 entries x 80 bytes (i16 type, i16 message_type, i16 skip, i16 x, i16 y, i16 width_blocks, i16 height_blocks, i16 image.id, i16 image.x, i16 image.y, 6 bytes skip, i16 title.x, i16 title.y, i16 subtitle.x, i16 subtitle.y, 4 skip, i16 video.x, i16 video.y, 14 skip, i32 urgent, i32 video_offset, 4 skip, i32 title_offset, i32 subtitle_offset, i32 content_offset), then the string data block (max 460000 bytes; offsets are relative to its start; offset 0 means NULL, so put a dummy byte at offset 0). Total file size must be 32024..492024 bytes and also <= 400000 (BUFFER_SIZE used for reading). Strings are NUL-terminated, Windows-1252 for English. | Augustus: load_augustus_messages() starts at index 321 and uses the first entry whose content offset is 0; it then writes 40 consecutive entries (321..360 when 321 is empty), which correspond to city_message_get_text_id() for MESSAGE_SOLDIERS_STARVING(122)..MESSAGE_ROUTE_PRICE_CHANGE(161). So entries 321..399 must have content offset 0. help_id 330 (ships) therefore shows an Augustus entry; nothing we can set. Editor ids 331/332 live in c3_map_mm.eng, not here. | Text id mapping: city message type t -> text id t+99 if t<=50 else t+199. Mission briefings: 200 + campaign mission (0..21). Building help: c->help_id in window/building/*.c; 0 falls back to 10. | Rich text (graphics/rich_text.c): '@P' = new paragraph (line break + indent), '@L' = line break, '@G<n>' = embed image GROUP_MESSAGE_IMAGES + n - 1 centred on its own lines, '@<digits><word>' = hyperlink to message id <digits>; the link text is the single following word (up to the next space) drawn in the red link font. Codes must begin a word (preceded by a space or at string start), e.g. 'end. @PNext'. A literal '@' cannot be written. Leading spaces of a line are dropped. | There is NO placeholder substitution inside content. Dynamic values are drawn by message_dialog.c in the header area of the inner panel instead: every non-tutorial city message shows month/year and 'To <player name>' (lang 63,5); DISASTER with param1 shows building type name (or denarii for id 251); TRADE_CHANGE shows resource icon + empire city name; PRICE_CHANGE shows resource icon + amount; ROUTE_PRICE_CHANGE shows city name + amount; EMIGRATION shows the low-mood cause text (lang group 12, cause+2); IMPERIAL appends request amount, resource icon/name and months remaining after the content. Content therefore refers to these indirectly ('shown above'). | Layout: dialog coordinates are a 640x480 space; BLOCK_SIZE = 16 px; panel is width_blocks x height_blocks at (x, y). Title is centred at y+14 (tutorial messages: y + title.y), text area starts at y+48 (pushed below image/subtitle). Subtitle is drawn only when subtitle.x != 0 (multiline at x+subtitle.x, y+subtitle.y). Text area height = height_blocks - 1 - (32 or 48 for manual + y_text - y)/16 blocks; width = width_blocks - 4 (+2 if no scrollbar). City message content starts 56 px (general) or 86 px (disaster/invasion/trade/price/emigration) into the inner panel, so keep those short. image.id: 0 = none; otherwise image_group(GROUP_MESSAGE_IMAGES) + id - 1 drawn at (x+image.x, y+image.y) (id 0 'about' uses GROUP_BIG_PEOPLE). All images set to null here to avoid depending on message pictures. video: smk path; played only if the file exists and the message pops up; all null here. urgent = 1 plays the urgent fanfare. message_type DISASTER/INVASION mark a 'problem' (go-to-problem button). Extra keys title_x/title_y/subtitle_x/subtitle_y are given per entry for the binary fields of the same name.
